components.name: Auto Section
components.summary: Works out the risers for you. Give it the tread depths and the minimum C-value you want to hold, and it raises each step by the smallest Riser Step increment that still clears that C-value - the shallowest bowl that meets the target. The front row starts on the start line, so wire the same field, focal point and start line that Section takes. Bake tread_lines if you want to fine-tune the steps by hand in Section afterwards.

inputs.name: Rows Per Tier
inputs.desc: How many steps each tier has, front row included - one per tier. Two is the minimum (no default - you set this)

inputs.name: Front Treads

inputs.name: Other Treads
inputs.desc: Depth of every step above the front one - one per tier (no default - you set this)

inputs.name: Tier Step Back
inputs.desc: How far the tier behind starts back from the last nosing below - one per gap between tiers. Negative reaches out over it (no default - you set this)

inputs.name: Tier Step Up
inputs.desc: How high the tier behind starts above the last nosing below - one per gap between tiers (no default - you set this)

inputs.name: Minimum C-Values
inputs.desc: The C-value every row must hold - one per tier, or one for all (default 90 mm)

inputs.name: Minimum Riser
inputs.desc: Shallowest riser to build. Front rows needing less get raised to it (default 150 mm)

inputs.name: Maximum Riser
inputs.desc: Tallest riser to build. Rows needing more get capped and warned. 0 = no cap (default 550 mm)

inputs.name: Eye Horizontal Offset
inputs.desc: How far back from the nosing a seated spectator's eye sits (default 150 mm)

inputs.name: Eye Vertical Offset
inputs.desc: Eye height above the tread, seated spectator (default 1200 mm)

inputs.desc: How far the first step sits in front of the focal point. Used only when Base Line is unwired

inputs.desc: Thickness of the stand slab. Set it once here - everything downstream reads it (default 200 mm)

components.name: Opening Cut

inputs.name: Seat Result
inputs.desc: The layout to open up. Wire from Seat SRD, or from a Cut to stack them

inputs.name: Cut Curve
inputs.desc: A CLOSED curve in plan - everything inside it is opened up. Open curves are ignored

inputs.name: Opening From
inputs.desc: One axis number per opening. Order does not matter - the span runs the short way, never wrapping past axis 0 (no default)

inputs.name: Opening To
inputs.desc: The other axis number of each opening, matching Opening From item for item (no default)

inputs.name: Rows
inputs.desc: How many treads each opening removes, counting up from the bottom of the tier - one per opening, so opening 1 can cut 3 rows while opening 2 cuts 10 (default 0)

inputs.name: Opening Type Mode
inputs.desc: SPAN empties the whole width, VOM cuts a rectangle at the midpoint - one per opening (default SPAN)

inputs.name: Cut Combine Mode
inputs.desc: With both openings and a curve set: BOTH cuts either, or use only one (default BOTH)

inputs.name: Opening Widths
inputs.desc: Width of a VOM opening - one per opening, ignored by SPAN (default 1200 mm)

inputs.name: Min Tread Depth
inputs.desc: Where a curve leaves a tread shallower than this, its seats go too. 0 = off (default 0)

inputs.name: Tier Enabled
inputs.desc: Which tiers these openings cut through. Empty = every tier (default true)

inputs.name: Panel Values

components.name: C-value Legend
components.summary: Builds an explicit colour legend for the C-value maps. Set the first number, the last number and the band size - the bands become <min, min to min+step, ... , >=max, each with its own colour. components.name: Data Gate
components.summary: Holds the wire shut. Whatever changes upstream, nothing downstream recomputes until you press PASS - then the data at D goes through R once and stays there. Put it between the 2D bowl chain and the heavy 3D build or analysis components: edit the bowl lag-free, press to update. The Gate Switch component opens and closes every gate on the canvas at once. components.name: Section Plus
components.summary: Adds the things a bare section does not have: the front barrier or handrail, accessible (wheelchair) rows, and the sightline check over the barrier.

components.name: Table Section
components.summary: Builds the tier sections from the numbers in your workbook instead of lines you draw.

components.name: Stand 2D
components.summary: Sweeps each tier section around the axis planes and flattens it into tread rings in plan.

components.name: Vomitory
components.summary: Places the vomitories — the tunnels spectators enter the bowl through — in the tread rings, and sets how each one gets down to the concourse: flat, stepped, stair or ramp.

components.name: Seat
components.summary: Fills the tread rings with seats, breaking each row at the vomitories and aisles, and flags rows that break the egress limits.

components.name: Custom Seat
components.summary: Same seat placement as Seat, but the vomitories, aisles and even the seats come from curves you draw instead of being generated.

components.name: Cut
components.summary: Cuts the bowl to shape — keep or remove a whole span between two axis numbers, or everything on one side of a curve you draw.

components.name: Opening Cut
components.summary: Punches local entrance openings through the stand — between two axis numbers, or under a closed curve you draw.

components.name: Stand 3D
components.summary: Sweeps the closed section profile around the axis planes into the solid tier bodies.

components.name: Vom 3D
components.summary: Builds the vomitories as solids — the side and end walls, the portal opening punched through, and the stair or ramp down to the concourse.

components.name: Stand 3D Plus
components.summary: Builds the 3D bowl: cuts the stand solids with everything the 2D chain decided — shape cuts, entrance openings, vomitories — and lifts the seats and aisle steps to their real tread heights.

components.name: Rail 3D
components.summary: Builds the railings and parapets as solids — the front barrier, the rear parapet, the edges left by a cut, and the walls around entrance openings.

components.name: Assemble Bowl
components.summary: Assembles the final bowl plan before Stand 3D Plus: merges parallel seat layouts (tiers renumbered), pulls exposed cut ends past their axis by the offset, and previews the finished plan.

components.name: Seat 3D
components.summary: Puts a chair and a seated spectator target on every seat of the built bowl.

components.summary: Paints every seat with its own C-value, measured in 3D from that seat's eye to its own focus.

recipes.label: Check one section
recipes.note: The shortest useful chain. Draw the field, set the axes, solve a section and read the C-value straight off it — no 2D layout, no solids.

recipes.label: The standard bowl
recipes.note: The backbone. Section to 2D layout to solids, with vomitories and a cut. Every other combination below is this one with something added.

recipes.label: Axes you draw yourself
recipes.note: Same chain, but the axes come from curves you drew instead of the automatic spacing. Everything downstream is unchanged — it cannot tell the difference.

recipes.label: Section from a workbook
recipes.note: Riser and tread numbers come out of Excel instead of a solved section, and the results go back to the sheet.

recipes.label: Railings on the stand
recipes.note: Adds railings to the built bowl. Their geometry feeds the sightline checks, so a rail that blocks a view shows up as a failed seat rather than a surprise on site.

recipes.label: Sightlines, seat by seat
recipes.note: Measures the C-value from every seat's own eye to its own focus and paints the result, then lays it out on a drawing sheet.

recipes.label: Section sheets
recipes.note: Takes one representative section per axis gap and flips through them on sheets — light enough to leave on while you tune the section.

recipes.label: Real chairs
recipes.note: Replaces the seat markers with chair geometry, so the model is presentable rather than diagrammatic.

recipes.label: Two sections, one bowl
recipes.note: Two different sections are cut to complementary spans and assembled into a single bowl. This is the combination that exercises joining, and the seat counts add up.
